//: tulip.computer. The site itself is stage/ (site/index.html + the shared
marketing assets); /run is the Tulip 1 web app; /2 is TULIP 5, which
lives in a repo and a Vercel project of its own and is PROXIED here.
WHY A PROXY RATHER THAN A COPY. Tulip 5's web build is content-stamped
and deployed by its own repo on every push (tulip5-web.vercel.app). A
path on this domain that served a COPY would be a second deploy anybody
has to remember, which is the exact way a stale wasm shipped once
already. A rewrite means tulip.computer/2 is whatever that project last
deployed, with no step in between. Vercel does not do path-based domain
assignment, so a rewrite is also the only way to put two projects on one
hostname.
THE TRAILING SLASH IS LOAD-BEARING. Tulip 5's index.html asks for
its loader and its wasm by RELATIVE name (`./micropython-<hash>.mjs`,
`micropython-<hash>.wasm`), so at /2 those resolve against the
DOMAIN ROOT and 404; at /2/ they resolve to /2/... and proxy
through. 307 rather than 308: a permanent redirect is cached by the
browser for ever and this is one of the few things here that might
still move.
THE ADMIN COMES FIRST, because /2/:path* would otherwise swallow it.
Vercel takes the first matching rewrite. It is the world service
that serves it: one page, one HTTP Basic gate, and the friend half
proxied server-side (see server/world_api.py) so the whole panel is
ONE origin and one password.
The catch-all no-cache, and /2 IS EXCLUDED FROM IT. Tulip 5's own
vercel.json already answers this question for its files — index.html
no-store, the content-stamped micropython-<hash>.{mjs,wasm}
immutable for a year — and those headers come through the proxy. A
no-cache stamped over the top would make every visit revalidate 8 MB
that is guaranteed by its own NAME never to change, which is the
whole point of stamping it.
